articles.title: Restoration of Historic Packer Spout Steps Completed in Rochdale Town Centre
articles.excerpt: The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, over 400 years old, has been completed, linking Rochdale Town Hall to St Chad’s Church, enhancing the town's historic landscape.
articles.content_html:
The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a unique set of historic steps over 400 years old, has been completed in Rochdale town centre. These steps, which run through the Broadfield Park Slopes, connect the major historic attractions of Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, which has parts dating back to Saxon times.

Dating from before 1660, the steps have a rich history, believed to have been used by mourning relatives who would ascend to St Chad’s Church to scatter rue and rosemary in the churchyard as offerings for their loved ones. The steps are situated in the recently restored Broadfield Park Slopes area, which during the Victorian period was known for its notorious slum, referred to as 'the gank'. This area was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, and high crime rates, with many residents working in Rochdale’s mills.

The restoration project was undertaken by Oldham contractor Maysand, who faced significant challenges due to the steepness of the site. A special pulley system with tracks and rollers was devised to transport the stone up the hill. The team meticulously removed all 122 steps, many of which were broken and uneven, before reconstructing the area underneath and the damaged steps using traditional sandstone to match the existing stone.

The completion of this restoration not only preserves a significant piece of Rochdale's history but also enhances the town's landscape, making it more accessible for residents and visitors alike. The steps are expected to attract more foot traffic between the town hall and St Chad’s Church, contributing to the local heritage tourism.

These events aim to raise awareness about the various forms of cyber crime, which can have serious consequences for victims, including financial loss and identity theft.

According to GMP, cyber crime encompasses a wide range of fraudulent activities, from identity theft and online transaction scams to dating fraud. The police highlighted that millions of cases of fraud and computer misuse are reported annually, many of which could be avoided by adopting better online habits.

Residents are encouraged to attend these events to learn practical steps to protect themselves from becoming victims of cyber crime. Simple measures, such as not sharing passwords or personal information and creating strong, unique passwords, can significantly reduce the risk of falling prey to online scams.

Greater Manchester Police are appealing for information following the alleged rape of a young man on Milnrow Road in Rochdale on August 16. CCTV images have been released as part of the investigation.

Greater Manchester Police are investigating an alleged rape of a young man that occurred in Rochdale on Sunday, August 16, 2026. Officers responded to reports of the incident at approximately 11.30am, with the areas of Milnrow Road and Newbold Street identified as significant to the investigation.

In an effort to gather more information, police have released CCTV images of a man they wish to speak to regarding the incident. Authorities believe this individual may have valuable information that could assist with their enquiries.

Anyone with information is urged to contact Greater Manchester Police by calling 101 and quoting log number 1763 of 16/08/2026. Alternatively, information can be submitted via the LiveChat function on the GMP website or by contacting Crimestoppers anonymously at 0800 555 111.

The police are keen to hear from anyone who may have witnessed the incident or has information that could aid the investigation. The release of CCTV images is part of their ongoing efforts to ensure justice is served.

articles.title: New Play Area Under Construction in Alkrington as Improvements Continue
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has commenced work on a new play area at Mainway Meadows in Alkrington, alongside enhancements to existing facilities at Sandy Park and Kirkway Stocks Play Park.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has begun construction on a new play area at Mainway Meadows, located between Mainway and Moss Way in Alkrington. The project aims to provide a safe and inclusive space for children of various ages and abilities, featuring accessible pathways, safety fencing, and a range of play equipment including swings, a slide, seesaw, roundabout, seating, and a children’s picnic table.

The work at Mainway Meadows is expected to take approximately four to five weeks to complete. This initiative is funded by Middleton Township, which aims to enhance play facilities for local families and create a welcoming environment for children.

In addition to the new play area, improvements to the existing play area at Sandy Park are nearing completion. Councillor Dylan Williams expressed enthusiasm about the new equipment being installed at Kirkway Stocks Play Park, also known as Farmway or Sandy Park, which will further enrich the recreational options available to residents.

These developments reflect the council's commitment to enhancing community spaces and ensuring that children in Alkrington have access to quality play facilities. Local families can look forward to enjoying these upgraded amenities in the coming weeks.

articles.excerpt: Pakistan has informed UK officials, including Ed Miliband, that it will not accept the return of Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison.

Pakistan has informed UK officials, including Ed Miliband, that it will not accept the return of Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison.

Pakistan has officially rejected the United Kingdom's request to repatriate Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, who was released from prison on July 2, 2026. The announcement came during a meeting between Ed Miliband, the UK Labour Party leader, and Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister.

During the discussions, Dar stated that there is no bilateral agreement between the UK and Pakistan that would allow for the transfer of individuals convicted of serious crimes, such as child sexual exploitation. He emphasised that Pakistan currently lacks the legislative framework to facilitate such repatriations, stating, "We currently do not have any legislation or formal mechanism under which we can take him back."

The UK government has been under pressure to address the situation, as it continues to fund Ahmed's probation terms, which reportedly cost thousands of pounds. The diplomatic discussions have highlighted the complexities of international law regarding the repatriation of convicted criminals, particularly in cases involving serious offences.

As it stands, the UK may need to consider alternative arrangements or negotiations if it wishes to resolve the issue of Ahmed's status. The situation remains fluid, and further diplomatic efforts may be required to address the implications of Ahmed's release and the UK's ongoing responsibilities.

articles.title: New Tesco Express Opens on Oldham Road in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A new Tesco Express store has opened its doors on Oldham Road, Rochdale, creating 13 jobs and offering various community initiatives.
articles.content_html:
A new Tesco Express store has opened today, August 28, on Oldham Road in Rochdale. The store features an in-store bakery, a food-to-go section, a Costa Coffee machine, an ATM, parking facilities, and InPost lockers.

The opening of the store has created 13 jobs, with eight new colleagues joining Tesco for the first time. Tesco is also encouraging local schools and community projects to apply for its Free Fruit & Veg for Schools programme, which provides grants of up to £1,500 to promote healthy eating among children.

Additionally, customers can support local causes by using blue Tesco tokens to vote for community projects at the store exit. Three projects will be featured in each funding round, with grants awarded based on the number of tokens received.

The Rochdale store participates in the Tesco Community Food Connection scheme, donating surplus food to charities and community groups at the end of each day, further supporting local initiatives.

articles.title: Roadworks Scheduled for Nowell Road and Pershore Road in Middleton on 26 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on The Esplanade will commence on 4 October 2026, resulting in temporary road closures.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that roadworks on The Esplanade will begin on 4 October 2026. The works will involve a temporary closure of part of The Esplanade, starting at the junction with St Mary's Gate and extending 20 metres east along the road.

The exact timing of the roadworks will depend on weather conditions, and they are expected to take place overnight. The council will provide signage on site to inform residents and motorists of the confirmed start date prior to the works commencing.

During the closure, there will be no alternative route available for vehicles. However, a marshal will be present on site to facilitate safe access to nearby car parks for residents and visitors.

Motorists and residents should plan their journeys accordingly and remain alert for updates from Rochdale Borough Council regarding the roadworks. For further information, a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester can be viewed on the council's website.
